quote.text: The signal is the truth. The noise is what distracts us from the truth.
quote.author: Nate Silver, The Signal and the Noise (2012)

stories.headline: A Speed King and an Accuracy King, Both Sized for the Card You Own
stories.dek: In forty-eight hours, NVIDIA and Meta each shipped a thirty-billion-parameter open model built to run on a single consumer GPU. Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is the fastest thing on the bench; Muse Glimmer is the sharpest. The community verdict is already written — and it is not "which is best," but "which is best for what."

stories.headline: The Band Everyone Left, and the Hobby That Wouldn't Die With It
stories.dek: Shortwave listening should be dead. The great international broadcasters have fled the band for a decade — the BBC to North America, Radio Australia entirely, the Voice of America's transmitters going dark last year. And yet the hobby is cheaper and, by some measures, larger than ever, because the price of entry collapsed from a US$200 receiver to a US$30 USB stick. This is a descent into a band of static, and the people who still tune it.

stories.headline: The Company You Can Carry
stories.dek: In the world's oldest, most single-person society, grown adults have turned plush toys into portable companions — carried to cafés and shrines, tucked into hotel beds, photographed everywhere with their owners' faces kept out of frame. It has a name, nuikatsu, and a fast-growing economy behind it. The West hasn't written it up yet. It will.

stories.headline: Kyiv Hands Washington a Plan No One Will Read Aloud
stories.dek: Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukraine has "conveyed its proposals to the American side" and is ready for "all negotiation formats." The content stays sealed; the American envoys have not been to Kyiv since January; and the only number that governs the war — the map — has not moved a metre. A fresh diplomatic push, or the theatre of one.

stories.kicker: Singapore · The Boom You Can't Feel
stories.headline: The Forecast Doubled. The Question Is Why Nobody Noticed.
stories.dek: On 11 August the Trade Ministry more than doubled its 2026 growth forecast to 4.5–5.5%, on an AI-driven electronics-export surge that pushed non-oil exports up 27% in the quarter. It is a genuine boom — and it is landing in a country where retrenchments are rising and the resale flat is falling. The gap between the print and the pavement is where this desk sits.

stories.headline: A Record Land Bid and a Falling Flat, in the Same Week
stories.dek: The state awarded the Bayshore Drive site at S$1,323 per square foot — the highest land rate ever paid outside the central region. Days later, the July HDB resale flash showed prices falling for a second straight quarter even as volume hit a 2026 high. Confidence at the top, softening in the middle: for an owner weighing the exit, both are the market.

stories.headline: A Foldable Goes Two-Nanometre — and the Hinge Asks the Buy-Once Question
stories.dek: Google's 12 August event led with the Pixel 11 Pro Fold at US$1,899: a Tensor G6 on TSMC's 2nm process, an eight-inch inner display, and a seven-year software promise. It is the longest-supported foldable of the cycle — and the one component you can't spec your way past is the fold itself.

stories.kicker: The Good Life · A Watch With a Livery
stories.headline: A Square German Chronograph for the Price of a Good Watch, Not a Grail
stories.dek: Union Glashütte's Averin Chronograph "Sachsen Classic 2026" is a 41mm racing-liveried square in steel at €3,700, limited to 350 pieces and timed to a vintage-car rally. It is a genuinely well-made value-luxury object — and the livery, not the movement, is what you're paying for. That's the appeal, and the tell.

stories.kicker: Screen & Sound · The Room and the Reviews
stories.headline: Two Comedies for Grown-Ups Died on the Same Weekend
stories.dek: A Will Gluck rom-com and a Broken Lizard sequel both opened soft, reviving the "theatrical comedy is dead" verdict — even as one of them posted an audience score well above its critics'. Meanwhile the acclaim for Phoebe Bridgers runs ahead of a single fan who's heard the record. Two gaps between the number and the room.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · The Lever That Actually Moves
stories.headline: Parents Fixate on Screens. The Research Points at Sleep.
stories.dek: A new analysis of more than 6,000 children aged 10 to 13 finds that of four lifestyle levers — sleep, screen time, activity, diet — sleep is by far the strongest link between a child's mental-health symptoms and how they actually do at school and with friends. The thing parents watch is not the thing that moves. General guidance, not medical advice.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Scare That Didn't Arrive
stories.headline: The Market Braced for a Hot Print. It Got a Mild One — and Gold Rose Anyway.
stories.dek: July US inflation came in at 3.4%, in line and cooler than June; the odds of a September rate hike fell, and ten-year yields eased. Yet gold pushed toward US$4,500 and bitcoin went nowhere. The same benign data priced three assets in three directions — which is the whole lesson.

stories.kicker: Fitness · The Count and the Dose
stories.headline: One Long Walk a Week Did What Three Shorter Ones Did
stories.dek: A randomised trial found that packing a week's brisk interval walking into a single 75-minute session cut body fat and lifted fitness about as much as splitting the same total time across three. The frequency you schedule matters less than the dose inside it — with caveats worth reading. General guidance, not medical advice.

stories.headline: One Alarm to Set This Morning, Then an October Worth Booking Flights For
stories.dek: BIGBANG's general sale drops today, Thursday, ahead of a Kallang October that stacks an F1 weekend and a sold-out December. In Japan, the autumn art calendar and the foliage windows reward booking the rooms now. Lock the tickets before the diaries fill.
